verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Kota stone processors with domestic order books and clean GST; avoid export-only units and those with retrenchment or unpaid wage signals.
title: Kota stone, granite & marble processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Kota stone is quarried and cut locally, then sold as slabs and tiles into construction demand; cash comes from converting block into finished slab and moving it fast.** Value sits in the quarry-to-polishing spread and in the working-capital cycle, not in the machine. Capex is modest and largely self-funded; the real risk is receivables and inventory sitting in the yard. **So when a proposal lands, check the split between domestic and export sales and the age of inventory before anything else.**

## What has changed now
**The local signal is weak: Rajasthan GST collections are -4.7% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand is +4.0% against India +9.5% [D].** That is a demand and activity gap, not a rounding error. Local reporting says West Asia war has hit Rajasthan exports, with factories near closure and falling orders [3], and a Kota stone shipper retrenched 60 workers without notice [2]. **So if a proposal is export-heavy, ask for the buyer-country mix and the last three months' order book; if the unit has cut staff, ask for wage arrears and PF dues.** The CM has announced encouragement for state mining and a royalty cut on marble, granite and limestone [1], but that report is old and the relief is policy intent, not cash.

## Where the growth is
**India-wide stone output is +11.4% YoY and +10.2% Apr-to-date [D], so the national pull is real even as Kota lags.** Peer Midwest shows granite volumes recovering quarter-on-quarter with blended ASP at INR60,792/cbm [4], and domestic plus China demand cited as strong [7]. **Pursue Kota processors with domestic institutional and builder orders, own or leased quarry linkage, and a clean GST trail; avoid pure export units and single-buyer shops.** Aro's June 2026 quarter net sales fell 23.72% YoY to Rs 20.62 crore [6] — that is the export-exposed template to stay away from.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the yard.** Take monthly GST returns, electricity bills and a stock statement; covenant a minimum DSCR and a receivables cap. **If fund-based utilisation crosses 56% of sanctioned limits [8], ask for the order book and buyer ageing.** Rating reports flag geographical concentration in Europe as a constraint [9], so cap export exposure. **Collect from customer: quarry lease terms, royalty paid, and buyer-wise sales mix.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch electricity consumption, GST filing regularity and wage payments monthly.** A drop in power draw with flat sales means stock is piling up; a missed GST filing means cash is short. **If retrenchment or unpaid wages appear, freeze fresh limits and review the account.**
